qt6_migration.pulse_latency_msec_overrides_qt_buffer_a: Qt6's PulseAudio sink (QPulseAudioSinkStream::startStream, src/multimedia/pulseaudio/qpulseaudiosink.cpp) sets pa_buffer_attr.maxlength to m_hardwareBufferFrames.value_or(1024) frames and leaves tlength at -1. maxlength is the server's whole buffer for the stream and PulseAudio clamps tlength down to it, so every Qt audio stream runs on 21ms at 48kHz. m_hardwareBufferFrames (m_nativePeriodFrames in dev) is only ever set by the spatial audio engine, unreachable from QAudioSink/QSoundEffect, so the 1024 fallback always applies. No public API reaches it: setBufferSize() and setBufferFrameCount() size Qt's own ringbuffer. Symptom is continuous chopping on slow single-core devices (1182 implicit underruns in 64s on beluga, 997 on sturgeon). THE FIX IS NOT A QT PATCH. PULSE_LATENCY_MSEC is read by LIBPULSE, not Qt (qtmultimedia 6.11.2 contains no reference to it): patch_buffer_attr() in src/pulse/stream.c, called from pa_stream_connect_playback(), DISCARDS the pa_buffer_attr the application supplied and substitutes maxlength=-1, tlength=<ms>, minreq=-1, prebuf=-1, fragsize=tlength, and forces PA_STREAM_ADJUST_LATENCY. So qputenv("PULSE_LATENCY_MSEC", ...) in main() before the sink starts fixes an individual app with no library change, which is what shipped (moWerk/asteroid-beatfork#4); meta-asteroid#318 patched qtmultimedia fleet-wide and was closed as too low level. Only asteroid-beatfork uses Qt for audio playback in a shipped image; everything else goes through ngfd/GStreamer. Geometry constraint either way: tlength must stay well under Qt's ringbuffer (0.4-0.5 measured best), because PulseAudio requests a whole tlength per callback, so equal sizes let one callback drain the ringbuffer and Qt then pads the shortfall with SILENCE and writes a full buffer anyway - audible, and invisible to PulseAudio because no underrun is reported. Cost of a longer buffer: an amplitude envelope applied at stop only ramps newly generated samples, so the already-queued tail (ringbuffer + tlength) plays at full volume first; size any drain timer as ring + tlength + ramp + margin or the tail is cut into a click.

app_launching_from_qml.pattern: To launch other AsteroidOS apps from QML, create an AppLauncher class in main.cpp with Q_INVOKABLE methods and expose via setContextProperty
app_launching_from_qml.implementation: class AppLauncher : public QObject with launchApp(QString) and launchDesktopFile(QString) methods using QProcess::startDetached()
app_launching_from_qml.lipstick_limitation: Lipstick.compositor.launchApplication() not accessible from community apps — Lipstick object undefined in QML runtime. Community apps cannot use the launcher's native app launching API.
app_launching_from_qml.qt_openUrlExternally_broken: Qt.openUrlExternally() fails with 'platform plugin does not support services' error on AsteroidOS — cannot be used for app launching
app_launching_from_qml.qprocess_requirement: #include <QProcess> and #include 'main.moc' when defining Q_OBJECT class directly in main.cpp
app_launching_from_qml.desktop_file_handling: Strip .desktop suffix from filename and launch the base name — full desktop file parsing not required for basic launching

community_app_packaging.single_page_app_root: Declare DisplaySettings and the page component directly inside Application root in main.qml. No AppShell, no Loader, no LayerStack.
community_app_packaging.appshell_black_screen: AppShell/Loader/LayerStack pattern causes silent black screen with no console errors on single-page apps — do not use. LayerStack silently swallows the page. Confirmed failure mode on asteroid-pulsar and asteroid-heliograph. Only use AppShell+LayerStack for genuine multi-page apps with push/pop navigation.
community_app_packaging.deferred_loading_pattern: For multi-page apps: Loader active: index === 0 || pagesWarmed. pagesWarmed set by 1500ms Timer.
community_app_packaging.writable_paths: Apps run as ceres user without root — all file writes must target XDG user-writable paths (~/.local/share/, ~/.config/), not /usr/share/
community_app_packaging.display_settings_in_main: For single-page apps declare DisplaySettings directly in Application root. No need to defer to AppShell.

qmake_submodule_in_cmake.pattern: When an app depends on a qmake-based library (e.g. literm), build it via add_custom_command inside CMakeLists.txt rather than migrating its build system. Invoke qmake + make targeting the submodule .pro file, output to CMAKE_BINARY_DIR/submodule-build/. Install the resulting plugin directory to ${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/lib/qml/<pluginname>/.
qmake_submodule_in_cmake.import_path: Call engine.addImportPath(QStringLiteral("/usr/lib/qml")) in main.cpp before engine.load() so the QML engine finds third-party plugins installed outside the default Qt plugin search paths.
qmake_submodule_in_cmake.install_target: Plugin directory must contain both the .so and a qmldir file. Install as a directory, not individual files, to preserve the qmldir alongside the binary.

community_app_packaging.new_repo_workflow: gh repo create moWerk/asteroid-appname --public --description '...' then git remote add origin git@github.com:moWerk/asteroid-appname.git && git push -u origin main

watchface_settings_page_pattern.description: Watchfaces can expose an embedded settings page via a Component property named settingsPage. The WatchfaceSelector detects this at runtime via typeof previewQml.item.settingsPage !== 'undefined' after the Loader has resolved. The settingsPage Component must be a self-contained Page with its own PageHeader. Detection requires the Loader to be active — previewQml.active must be true for the active watchface tile. dodoradio PR #87 introduced this pattern.
watchface_settings_page_pattern.push_pattern: layerStack.push(previewQml.item.settingsPage) — pushes the Component directly, no wrapper needed for stock watchfaces
watchface_settings_page_pattern.user_watchface_with_settings: Push WatchfaceSettingsContainer with settingsPage Component reference + watchfaceName + watchfaceFile params — container hosts both settings and remove page in horizontal ListView

watchface_xdg_user_path.description: User-installed watchfaces live in the XDG user data path, not the system path. WatchfaceHelper.userWatchfacePath() returns the plain path (no file:// prefix) to ~/.local/share/asteroid-launcher/watchfaces/. WatchfaceHelper.userAssetPath() returns the file:// prefixed URL to ~/.local/share/asteroid-launcher/. FolderListModel pointing at user watchfaces must prepend file:// to userWatchfacePath(). Active watchface dconf values for user watchfaces must use userAssetPath() + 'watchfaces/' + name + '.qml' to get the correct file:// prefix. Documentation must be updated to point users to XDG path for manual installs instead of the system path which requires root.

ungrabmouse_after_release_unnecessary.description: Calling ungrabMouse() inside mouseReleaseEvent is unnecessary per Qt 5.15 docs: there is no need to call this function after a release or cancel event since no future events will be received in any case. The GestureFilterArea PR adding ungrabMouse() after swipeReleased was rejected on this basis. If a contributor proposes ungrabMouse() in a release handler, request a concrete reproduction case demonstrating a stuck grab before accepting it.

quickpanel_pressdelay.description: pressDelay: 100 on the QuickPanel slidingRow ListView is confirmed working on device. 200ms is perceptibly slow as tap lag on the toggle buttons. 100ms is the correct value — long enough to let the Flickable distinguish flick from tap, short enough to not feel sluggish. Pair with preventStealing: true on QuickPanelToggle to prevent the ListView reclaiming the press after the delay resolves.

flickable_deceleration.description: Qt's default Flickable flickDeceleration was designed for phone-class DPI and screen sizes. On watch screens it produces over-travel that makes list position hard to predict after a flick. AsteroidOS currently does not tune this at all. Setting flickDeceleration per ListView instance is the pragmatic approach — it does not require patching the Qt platform plugin and avoids portability issues. A custom AsteroidOS ListView control in qml-asteroid that sets sensible defaults would be the correct long-term solution. No confirmed values yet — needs systematic measurement across device screen sizes.

new_app_desktop_generation.rule: asteroid-generate-desktop needs TWO inputs, not one: <src>/<app>.desktop.template AND <src>/i18n/<app>.desktop.h. Shipping only the template builds a package with no .desktop and no launcher entry.
new_app_desktop_generation.header_format: i18n/<app>.desktop.h must contain the default display name as a magic comment: //% "My App"  followed by qtTrId("id-app-launcher-name");  — the script extracts it with grep -oP '//% "\K[^"]+(?=")'
new_app_desktop_generation.failure_mode: With the header missing the generator exit 2s, no .desktop is written, and the build fails LATER in do_install with a bare 'CMake Error at cmake_install.cmake:<n> (file): No such file or directory' — no filename, no mention of the generator. Do not debug this as a CMake bug; read the generator's preconditions.
new_app_desktop_generation.harmless_message: 'Couldn't find a corresponding language id, aborting' with exit 0 is NORMAL for a new app with no i18n/*.ts translations yet. It reads like the error and is not.
new_app_desktop_generation.configure_time_trap: generate_desktop() runs at CMake CONFIGURE time via execute_process. Adding the header only takes effect once do_configure actually re-runs — devtool reuses a cached configure and reproduces the IDENTICAL error, which reads as 'the fix did nothing' when the fix never executed. Run 'bitbake -c cleansstate <app>' before any rebuild meant to prove a configure-time fix.
new_app_desktop_generation.cheap_verification: Verify a configure-time generator by running it by hand against the staged source before spending a build cycle: <sysroots-components>/x86_64/asteroid-generate-desktop-native/usr/bin/asteroid-generate-desktop <srcdir> <appname> /tmp/out.desktop
new_app_desktop_generation.devtool_does_not_package: devtool build <app> stops after do_packagedata: it reports full success and leaves deploy/ipk EMPTY. The installable package needs an explicit 'bitbake -c package_write_ipk <app>'.
new_app_desktop_generation.verified: 2026-07-28, benchymark on the w541 (Arch bare metal, native build). Package payload confirmed by unpacking the ipk.
new_app_desktop_generation.upstream_status: Reported to moWerk for co-maintainer discussion: the two-input requirement is undocumented, the failure surfaces far from its cause, and the empty-.ts message should not say 'aborting'.

filehelper_c_path_format.summary: The FileHelper C++ singleton contributed by beroset expects a native filesystem path, NOT a file:// URI. Correct: '/home/ceres/shopper.txt'. Incorrect: 'file:///home/ceres/shopper.txt'. XMLHttpRequest works with file:// URIs because it is URI-scheme-aware, but FileHelper uses QFile internally which expects native paths. Confirmed failure: 'No such file or directory' error when passing URI to FileHelper.writeFile().

persistence.qsettings_vs_dconf: QSettings for app-private state — part of QtCore, no CMakeLists or recipe changes needed. MGConfItem/dconf only when other apps may write the same key. Confirmed pattern: FlorentRevest explicitly recommended QSettings over dconf for stopwatch state because no other app changes timing values — cross-app reactivity was not needed.
persistence.mgconfitem_dep: mlite5 — avoid unless cross-app notification is genuinely needed
persistence.qsettings_group_separator: QSettings treats '/' in key as group separator — level1/bestTime maps to [level1] group with bestTime field
persistence.qsettings_singleton_pattern: C++ singleton registered via qmlRegisterSingletonType. Q_PROPERTY with READ/WRITE/NOTIFY for each field enables reactive QML bindings. WRITE setter calls m_settings.sync() and emits changed signal. QML can assign directly via property assignment without Q_INVOKABLE when WRITE is declared.
persistence.qsettings_invokable_only_pattern: For per-key data that is read once at event time rather than bound live (e.g. per-difficulty high scores), use Q_INVOKABLE read/write methods with no Q_PROPERTY and no NOTIFY signal. Avoids binding engine overhead for data QML never needs to watch reactively. Write guard (only store if value exceeds current) built into the invokable setter. Key mapping pattern: display string toLower().replace(' ', '_') + '/' + field — QSettings '/' separator produces clean INI sections automatically. Confirmed pattern: DodgerStorage.highScore(difficulty) / setHighScore(difficulty, v) in asteroid-dodger.
persistence.qsettings_migration_direction: Co-maintainers are actively migrating community apps away from Nemo.Configuration/mlite5 toward QSettings. New apps should use QSettings singleton from the start. Existing apps using ConfigurationValue should plan migration — mlite5 dependency may be dropped from meta-asteroid-community.
persistence.combo_persistence_lesson: Never maintain local QML property copies alongside C++ storage properties for the same state. They silently diverge. Use the singleton directly everywhere in QML.
persistence.file_read_singleton: For user-editable plain text files read at launch: slim read-only C++ singleton with Q_INVOKABLE method only, no write-back. QFile + QTextStream in the invokable. Registered via qmlRegisterSingletonType. File path hardcoded to /home/ceres/.local/share/appname/filename.txt. Recipe installs the default file via do_install:append with install -m 0644.
persistence.property_var_mutation_signal: Mutating a property var array (unshift, index assignment) does NOT emit a changed signal in Qt 5.15. Always reassign: categories = categories after mutation to force binding re-evaluation in dependent items.

opkg_no_overwrite.rule: opkg does NOT overwrite an existing file on device when reinstalling a package, even if the packaged version has different content. If the app previously created the file (even as empty), subsequent reinstalls leave that existing file untouched.
opkg_no_overwrite.implication: A recipe that installs a default data file via do_install:append is only reliable for truly clean installs. Any user who ran a broken prior version that caused the app to create the file (e.g. by writing empty content on startup) will never receive the corrected file through a package update.
opkg_no_overwrite.confirmed_case: asteroid-shopper 2.5: broken install caused FileHelper.writeFile to create an empty default-shopper.txt. Subsequent fixed-recipe reinstall left the empty file in place. Only a manual rm before reinstall resolved it.

default_data_file_seeding.rule: Shipping a default data file via recipe alone is not sufficient for resilience. The app must be self-healing: on startup, if the expected file exists but is empty, treat it the same as missing and reseed from a bundled fallback.
default_data_file_seeding.pattern: Bundle the default file in resources.qrc. On Component.onCompleted, after FileHelper.exists() check: if the file exists but countItems() returns 0, read the bundled default from Qt resources (:/default-shopper.txt) and write it via FileHelper.writeFile. Recipe still installs the file as a convenience for fresh installs, but the app does not depend on it.
default_data_file_seeding.why: Separates concerns correctly: recipe handles installation, app handles data integrity. Eliminates the opkg-no-overwrite failure mode permanently.

hardware.catfish_native_resolution_clarification: Catfish (TicWatch Pro) native screen resolution is 400x400px. The 240x240px canonical reference resolution in visual_design_guide.json is the Dims.l typography validation floor — the minimum screen size used to verify font legibility thresholds — not catfish's actual panel resolution. Dims.l(100) on catfish returns 400px. Confusing these two values is a confirmed LLM error mode.
hardware.device_hardware_database: device_db_final.json is the canonical combined hardware and feature reference for all AsteroidOS devices. It merges watches-support.json (AsteroidOS feature statuses), the community WearOS spec spreadsheet (hardware specs: resolution, DPI, screen type, RAM, battery, sensors), and the wiki Watch Feature List (authoritative feature statuses post-2.0 release). The Watch Feature List at https://wiki.asteroidos.org/index.php/Watch_Feature_List is the most authoritative and recent source for per-device feature statuses. Hardware absent from a device is represented as omitted from the features array (not listed as 'bad') — this is the semantic distinction between 'missing' (no hardware) and 'bad' (hardware exists, software not working).
hardware.gpu_monitoring: cat /sys/class/kgsl/kgsl-3d0/gpu_busy_percentage — reads Adreno GPU busy percentage. Use to baseline shader wallpaper GPU cost against FlatMesh at equivalent frame rate.
hardware.catfish: AsteroidOS flagship reference device, 9/10 performance rating. NOT the slowest. Primary development and performance gate.
hardware.rubyfish_rover_hoki: Marginally faster than catfish due to newer SoC (msm8937 vs msm8909w), tested secondary device
hardware.slow_devices: 2-3 watches appear slow due to Android base upgrade port issues, NOT hardware speed
hardware.screen_shapes: Three categories: round (majority — primary design target), square (dory-family — tolerate round content), rectangular-portrait (Beluga only — use Math.min(parent.width, parent.height) for all circular content)
hardware.60fps_game_loops: 16ms Timer game loops confirmed working on all current devices including catfish. 55+ per-rock Shape Repeaters with PathPolyline bindings updating every frame are acceptable load.
hardware.round_screen_hud_safety: HUD elements above 15% from top or below 85% from bottom risk clipping on round screens.

accelerometer_axes.confirmed_on_rubyfish_catfish: X positive = left edge dips (roll right). Y positive = screen tilts away from user (top edge dips = negative pitch in our convention). Z positive = face up flat.
accelerometer_axes.pitch_formula: Math.atan2(-smoothedY, Math.abs(smoothedZ)) * 180 / Math.PI — positive when top edge dips
accelerometer_axes.roll_formula: Math.atan2(smoothedX, Math.abs(smoothedZ)) * 180 / Math.PI — positive when left edge dips
accelerometer_axes.horizon_formula: Math.atan2(smoothedX, smoothedY) * 180 / Math.PI — gimbal-safe XY-only formula for horizon mode rotation. Confirmed stable at all angles including 90deg. Never use Z in horizon rotation formula — causes gimbal lock singularity at vertical orientation.
accelerometer_axes.smoothing_factor_spirit_level: 0.14 confirmed for spirit level use — slower than game use (0.65) for stability
accelerometer_axes.smoothing_factor_game: 0.65 confirmed for game use with dead zone 0.06
accelerometer_axes.smoothing_factor_message_rotation: 0.4 confirmed for heliograph message rotation — responsive enough for arm movement, stable enough to avoid jitter
accelerometer_axes.multi_orientation_horizon: ABANDONED — do not retry. Attempted horizonAxis detection to support nightstand/sideways orientation. Multiple atan2 formula switching approaches failed. Only user-facing tilt (Y-axis dominant) works reliably with the horizon formula. Root cause not fully diagnosed.

sendevent_touch_simulation.summary: On AsteroidOS devices (confirmed on sturgeon/Huawei Watch), touch input can be simulated over SSH using sendevent on /dev/input/event0 (synaptics_dsx driver). Uses Linux multi-touch protocol B. Key event codes: ABS_MT_TRACKING_ID (3/57), ABS_MT_POSITION_X (3/53), ABS_MT_POSITION_Y (3/54), ABS_MT_TOUCH_MAJOR (3/48), ABS_MT_TOUCH_MINOR (3/49), SYN_REPORT (0/0/0). Touch down: TRACKING_ID = positive integer. Touch up: TRACKING_ID = -1. Long press for AoD wake confirmed working at 0.8s hold. The 'input tap x y' command exists but crashes with core dump on AsteroidOS — use sendevent directly. /dev/input/event1 is qpnp_pon (power/key events), not touchscreen.

getevent_recording_replay.summary: Touch interaction sequences can be recorded using 'getevent -t /dev/input/event0 > tour.log' while performing gestures manually. The -t flag adds timestamps. An awk script can convert the timestamped log into a sendevent replay shell script by mapping hex event codes to sendevent commands and computing sleep durations from timestamp deltas. Useful for demo automation and regression testing without physical screen access. Replay via 'ssh root@watch bash -s < tour_replay.sh'.

community_recipe_cmake_access.summary: Community recipe sysroots DO have access to meta-asteroid CMake modules including ECM, AsteroidApp6, Asteroid6CMakeSettings, and Asteroid6Translations when qml-asteroid is in DEPENDS. The CMake configure step succeeds. The actual failure mode when using generate_desktop() without asteroid-generate-desktop-native in DEPENDS is at do_install time — cmake cannot find the generated appname.desktop file. Fix: add asteroid-generate-desktop-native to DEPENDS:append. The prior claim that these modules were unavailable in community sysroots was wrong. Confirmed by asteroid-toolwatch community recipe build, MagneFire clarification 2026-05.

qml_microphone_access_approaches.summary: Microphone access in AsteroidOS QML apps has two paths: (1) File-based: AudioRecorder from QtMultimedia records to WAV file, analyze periodically — pure QML, ~0.5-2s latency. (2) Real-time: QAudioInput + AudioProbe requires a C++ wrapper class exposing raw sample buffers to QML — enables BPM onset detection. For BPM detection from audio, simple energy-window onset detection (10ms windows, peak threshold ~1.5x neighbours) is viable on watch ARM hardware. Full FFT libraries are too heavy.

palm_to_sleep.description: Palm-to-sleep gesture requires a functional ambient light sensor. Covering the display blocks the sensor and triggers immediate sleep. Always active when the light sensor is present, no software toggle exists. Not available on watches where the light sensor hardware is absent or non-functional — check device feature list.

audio.format: WAV preferred, keep under 0.5s for clean PulseAudio buffer handling
audio.loop_splice: ensure whole number of cycles at target frequency to avoid click on loop

bluetooth_audio.classic_bt_mode: Edit /etc/bluetooth/main.conf and comment out 'ControllerMode = le' line to enable BR/EDR (classic Bluetooth) alongside BLE
bluetooth_audio.dual_mode_support: After enabling classic mode, watch supports both BLE sync (notifications, weather) and A2DP audio devices simultaneously
bluetooth_audio.runtime_toggle: Can toggle between BLE-only and dual-mode by editing config and restarting bluetooth service without full reboot
bluetooth_audio.a2dp_pairing: Use bluetoothctl to pair/trust/connect A2DP devices. Trusted devices auto-connect on power-on.
bluetooth_audio.battery_impact: Dual-mode Bluetooth increases battery consumption vs BLE-only mode
bluetooth_audio.gst_play_test: gst-play-1.0 /path/to/file.mp3 routes audio correctly to connected Bluetooth speaker via PulseAudio

mpd.audio_output_pulseaudio: type pulse, server unix:/run/user/1000/pulse/native, user ceres
mpd.systemd_service: mpd.service, must run as ceres user to access PulseAudio session
mpd.playlist_workflow: Files visible via 'listall' are NOT playable until added to current playlist with 'add /' command

mpd_mpris_bridge.purpose: Exposes MPD playback as an MPRIS2 D-Bus service — org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.mpd.asteroid
mpd_mpris_bridge.open_uri_missing: mpd-mpris does NOT implement the OpenUri D-Bus method — returns UnknownMethod error. Files must be queued via MPD protocol (add command) and playback triggered separately via Play.

mpd.mpris_manager_bluetooth_only: import org.nemomobile.mpris 1.0 — MprisManager only connects to Bluetooth MPRIS services (asteroid-btsyncd). Despite the general-sounding name it cannot control local MPRIS services like mpd-mpris. For local MPD control, use a separate DBusInterface targeting org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.mpd.asteroid or a native MpdUtil class.

mpd_mpris_recipe_final.supersedes: Earlier partial recipe captures — this is the confirmed-building version
mpd_mpris_recipe_final.vendor_requirement: go mod vendor must be run manually using go-binary-native binary before bitbake
mpd_mpris_recipe_final.parse_failure_cause: do_install:append with heredoc (cat > file << 'EOF') causes ParseError if EOF content has extra indentation or adjacent empty lines. Content after << 'EOF' must be flush-left.
mpd_mpris_recipe_final.chown_antipattern: chown username in do_install fails with 'invalid user' — use User=1000 in service file and tmpfiles.d for ownership
mpd_mpris_recipe_final.open_uri_not_implemented: mpd-mpris does NOT implement OpenUri D-Bus method — returns UnknownMethod. Cannot load files via D-Bus URI.

mpd.mixer_software_required: MPD volume control (setvol) fails with 'Failed to set mixer for AsteroidOS PulseAudio; disconnected' unless mixer_type "software" is explicitly set in /etc/mpd.conf. Without it, mpc volume commands appear to succeed but have no effect, and mpd-mpris volume property set produces a stacktrace. Fix: add mixer_type "software" to the audio_output block or as a top-level config key.
mpd.mpc_file_path_format: mpc add expects a relative path from music_directory OR a file:// URI with escaped spaces. Spaces in filenames must be quoted: mpc add "file:///home/ceres/music/Fonzee - Physicallost.mp3" or escaped with backslash.
mpd.go_binary_path: On AsteroidOS Yocto build: go-binary-native installs to build/tmp-glibc/work/x86_64-linux/go-binary-native/1.22.12/go/bin/go (note: no -r0 suffix in this path). GOROOT is at the same prefix: build/tmp-glibc/work/x86_64-linux/go-binary-native/1.22.12/go/lib/go (contains bin/, pkg/, src/).

gotchas: SoundEffect.GameRole does not exist in Qt 5.15 — app crashes immediately if set. Do not use.
SoundEffect pipeline priming (silent play on onLoadedChanged or toggle activation) causes audible ghost fires at unexpected moments — do not attempt pipeline warmup tricks.
SoundEffect.Infinite + rapid source swap causes PA stream conflicts
dual SoundEffect ping-pong causes drops/burps on PA
manual loop via Timer causes crackling
PA stream release timing unpredictable without mixer API

systemd_session_bus_access.problem: systemd services run with a bare environment — DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS is not set by default. Services that need the session D-Bus (e.g. any MPRIS bridge, any app communicating with ceres-owned services) will start without error but silently fail to register on the session bus.
systemd_session_bus_access.fix: Add to [Service] in the unit file: Environment="DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus"
systemd_session_bus_access.verification: cat /proc/$(pidof servicename)/environ | tr '\0' '\n' — confirms DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS is present in the running process environment
systemd_session_bus_access.session_bus_path: unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus — owned by ceres (UID 1000), permissions srw-rw-rw-
systemd_session_bus_access.confirmed_failure: mpd-mpris ran for 5+ hours as active/running with no errors but was absent from dbus ListNames — missing DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS was the sole cause

yocto_runtime_user_ownership.antipattern: chown ceres:ceres inside do_install — fails with 'invalid user: ceres:ceres' because the build sandbox has no knowledge of target system users
yocto_runtime_user_ownership.fix_service_user: Use User=1000 (UID) instead of User=ceres in systemd unit files embedded in recipes — avoids username resolution during install
yocto_runtime_user_ownership.fix_directory_ownership: Use systemd tmpfiles.d to set ownership at runtime. Install a file to ${D}${sysconfdir}/tmpfiles.d/pkgname.conf with: d /path/to/dir 0700 1000 1000 - and optionally Z /path/to/dir 0700 1000 1000 - for recursive enforcement. Add to FILES:${PN} and trigger via systemd-tmpfiles --create at boot.
yocto_runtime_user_ownership.tmpfiles_d_note: The Z directive sets ownership recursively on all children — needed when the service creates subdirectories at runtime. The d directive alone only affects the top-level directory.

missing_properties.serviceFilter: Does NOT exist — cannot restrict MprisManager to a specific service. Must manage currentService manually.
missing_properties.openUri_file_scheme: MprisManager.openUri() rejects file:// URLs — logs 'bool MprisController::openUri(const QUrl&) The scheme is not supported'. Only works for remote streaming URIs from Bluetooth MPRIS sources.

mprismanager_api.service_switching: Set currentService to an explicit service name string from availableServices to switch control target. Set to empty string ('') to disconnect. availableServices is a list of currently registered MPRIS service names on the session bus.
mprismanager_api.slot_error: QObject::connect: No such slot MprisPlayerInterface::onAsyncSetPropertyFinished(QDBusPendingCallWatcher*) — non-fatal warning appearing when a remote MPRIS service is active. Does not break remote metadata display or playback control.
mprismanager_api.bluetooth_service_name: org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.asteroid-btsyncd — the Bluetooth MPRIS bridge service name. This is what MprisManager picks up for remote device control.

cpp_singletons.q_property_pattern: Q_PROPERTY(type name READ getter WRITE setter NOTIFY changed). WRITE setter validates, writes to m_settings, calls sync(), emits signal. QML assigns directly without Q_INVOKABLE.
cpp_singletons.q_invokable_vs_property: Calling a non-invokable C++ method directly from QML JS throws silent TypeError that exits the calling function with no console output.
cpp_singletons.qsettings_in_constructor: Initialise QSettings in constructor initialiser list with full path. Call QDir().mkpath() for the config directory in constructor body.
cpp_singletons.clock_boottime: clock_gettime(CLOCK_BOOTTIME) — monotonic, ticks through suspend, resets on reboot.
cpp_singletons.clock_boottime_session_tracking: CLOCK_BOOTTIME for stopwatch/timer session tracking: store startBoottime = boottimeMs() on start(). On app restart, if boottimeMs() >= savedStartBoottime, same boot — resume with elapsed = baseElapsed + (boottimeMs() - startBoottime). If boottimeMs() < savedStartBoottime, reboot detected — invalidate session. Superior to /proc/uptime (no file read) and wall clock (immune to NTP/DST/manual changes). Confirmed pattern in asteroid-stopwatch StopwatchController.
cpp_singletons.reboot_detection: currentBoottime < savedStartBoottime is unambiguous reboot detection without UUID
cpp_singletons.read_only_singleton: For file-reading singletons with no write-back: Q_DISABLE_COPY, private default constructor, static qmlInstance factory, Q_INVOKABLE methods only. No Q_PROPERTY needed. See FileHelper pattern in asteroid-heliograph.

dbus_typed_call_boolean.issue: DBus typedCall boolean arguments must use JS boolean false/true, not string '0'/'1'. Passing { "type":"b", "value":"0" } silently sends incorrect data — confirmed bug found in TimezonePage SetTimezone call.

root_ssh_session_limitations.dconf: dconf requires a live user session with XDG_RUNTIME_DIR set. Root SSH sessions have no /run/user/0 dconf socket. Always run dconf commands as ceres: ssh ceres@catfish 'dconf write ...'
root_ssh_session_limitations.reboot: systemd-logind silently ignores reboot/shutdown from non-seat SSH sessions. ssh root@catfish 'reboot' works as a one-shot command. Interactive root shell reboot requires su root first to inherit a seat session.
root_ssh_session_limitations.su_from_root: su -s /bin/sh -c '...' ceres from a root SSH shell inherits root's broken environment, not ceres's session. XDG_RUNTIME_DIR override also fails due to /run/user/0 permission. Only a real ceres login gets a working session.

timedate1.list_timezones: timedateDbus.call('ListTimezones', undefined, callback) — callback receives flat string array
timedate1.set_timezone: timedateDbus.typedCall('SetTimezone', [{ type: 's', value: tzName }, { type: 'b', value: false }], successCb, errorCb)

dbus_patterns.firstrun_reset: dconf write /org/asteroidos/launcher/firstRunDone false — FirstRunConfig shows on next reboot
dbus_patterns.hardware_button_input: UNRESOLVED — no confirmed working pattern for hardware button press events in community apps. Root cause confirmed: evdev key events arrive at Lipstick compositor layer and are consumed there. Active Wayland surface never receives them because asteroid-launcher does not call QWaylandSeat::sendKeyPressEvent() for secondary buttons. Fix location is asteroid-launcher, not the app. Once forwarded, plain QML Keys.onPressed with focus: true works. Proposed canonical mapping: Qt::Key_Context1 as a neutral secondary button key. DeviceSpecs.hasSecondaryButton should be added to qml-asteroid once forwarding is implemented.

localization.array_strings: each //% comment must be on its own line immediately before the qsTrId() it annotates
localization.convention: toUpperCase at render time — translators write natural case
localization.pipeline: lupdate-qt5 to edit .ts to lrelease to .qm compiled into binary
localization.lupdate_command: lupdate-qt5 -no-obsolete src/* i18n/appname.desktop.h -ts i18n/appname.${lang}.ts — per the canonical pattern (asteroid-helloworld template) the .desktop.h lives in i18n/. Some older or manually reorganised apps placed it at the repo root; check the actual location before running.
localization.lupdate_name_tag_bug: generated .ts files may have <n></n> instead of <name></name> — fix: sed -i 's|<n></n>|<name></name>|g' i18n/*.ts
localization.lupdate_desktop_h: for apps with a .desktop.h file, reference it directly by path in lupdate call — glob i18n/*.h fails if file is in root
localization.lupdate_stacked_comments: Adjacent //% comments are concatenated by lupdate into a single mangled source string e.g. '//% "Edit List"' immediately followed by '//% "Edit Item"' produces source 'Edit ListEdit Item'. Each //% comment must sit on its own line directly above its own qsTrId() call — split ternary expressions across lines if necessary.
localization.lrelease_ampersand_escape: Bare & in any .ts translation string causes lrelease parse error: 'Expected # or [a-zA-Z], but got space'. All & characters in <translation> and <source> tags must be escaped as & — affects category names like 'Meat & Fish' and 'Baby & Pet'.
localization.default_category_translation: Default category names that are stored as user data should use qsTrId() at the property definition site so the active locale is applied on first launch. Once stored in config/files they become user data and are not re-translated on locale change — this is correct behaviour.
localization.untranslated_literals: SOS, CQD, XXX, MAYDAY, Emoji, Kaomoji, musical note names, Italian tempo names, Unicode symbols (snowflake etc.) — leave as string literals
localization.custom_user_strings: User-editable strings from plain text files are never translated — category keys in custom.txt are always English lowercase regardless of UI language
localization.ts_files_all_need_new_entries: When adding a new translated string, add its entry to EVERY i18n/*.ts file, not just the source locale. Other-language files carry the entry with an unpopulated (empty) <translation>; the release flow expects them all present. FlorentRevest, asteroid-flashlight PR #18 (de_DE.ts): 'Other translation files need the new entries too, just not populated with a translation.'

startup_performance.jit_preloader_implementation: Confirmed implementation: declare a hidden Item (visible: false) at the root level named 'preloader'. Inside it, place: (1) a Rectangle with a SequentialAnimation running at onCompleted to fire a flash path through the renderer, (2) an Image preloading the main player SVG with a SequentialAnimation on opacity, (3) a NonGraphicalFeedback with event: 'short' played in Component.onCompleted. The hidden Item forces the GPU shader pipeline to compile and the SVG to rasterize before the game scene is shown, eliminating the first-frame stutter. The 'short' haptic event is a side-effect of playing it — the actual warmup goal is the rendering pass. Pattern confirmed in asteroid-dodger v1.5 preloader.
startup_performance.irreducible_floor: ~700ms — libGLES context creation in vendor driver per Kido profiling
startup_performance.qml_parse_overhead: ~300ms — AppShell deferred load reduces this for multi-page apps
startup_performance.mapplauncherd: already running on AsteroidOS — confirmed via strace at /run/user/1000/mapplauncherd/qt5
startup_performance.yocto_source_date_epoch: new Date() in QML at build time reflects SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (Yocto reproducible builds timestamp — typically the last git commit in the metadata layers). Defaults to a value like 1520598896 (March 2018) that only changes when Yocto layers are upgraded. Without a working RTC, the watch boots at epoch 0 and systemd advances the clock to SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. This explains why FirstRunConfig date selector presets a date months or years in the past — the RTC default is not a Qt or AsteroidOS bug, it is an expected consequence of Yocto reproducible builds.
startup_performance.single_page_no_deferred_load: Single-page apps gain nothing from AppShell deferred loading — declare everything in main.qml directly

qt_515_limitations: Canvas ctx.shadowColor comma-operator bug: ctx.shadowColor = (r, g, b, a) uses the JS comma operator — evaluates all operands but assigns only the last value (a). Canvas shadows never work when set this way. Correct form: ctx.shadowColor = Qt.rgba(r, g, b, a).

fastblur_game_overlay_cost: QtGraphicalEffects.FastBlur applied to live game content is prohibitively expensive on AsteroidOS devices — causes severe frame drop during pause/game-over overlay transitions. Confirmed abandoned in asteroid-blaster after testing. Replacement: a plain Rectangle with color '#80000000' (50% opacity black), animated with a 250ms InOutQuad Behavior on opacity. Achieves the visual goal at near-zero GPU cost. Do NOT use FastBlur as a pause or overlay blur effect on game scenes.

Qt6 ShaderEffect no longer accepts inline GLSL strings for vertexShader/fragmentShader — requires pre-compiled .qsb files from the qsb tool. Any Qt5 code that injects GLSL strings into ShaderEffect.fragmentShader at runtime is architecturally invalid in Qt6 and must be rewritten as a C++ QQuickItem using QShaderBaker.

QShaderBaker (Qt::ShaderTools module) is the Qt6 runtime GLSL compiler — takes a GLSL string, returns a QShader object in memory without touching disk. Correct tool for user-supplied shaders unknown at build time. NOT appropriate for shaders known at build time (e.g. FlatMesh) where pre-compiled .qsb resources are correct. Requires Qt::ShaderTools to be included in the build — confirm with maintainers before depending on it.
NumberAnimation duration not settable as property after declaration — bind to page-level property
property var holding C++-backed QtObject refs unreliable in Connections
Behavior on visible not supported — use Timer + opacity for fade-then-hide
ColorAnimation on Text forces rasterization — prefer Rectangle overlay
Only one Component.onCompleted allowed per QML component
Multi-line ternary where newline precedes colon silently evaluates only first branch — all ternaries must be single-line
Behavior on font.pixelSize not supported — snaps only
SequentialAnimation on a property takes permanent ownership — declarative binding on same property breaks after first run
Per-corner radius not supported on Rectangle — single radius only
clip on Rectangle clips to bounding box not to radius shape
Repeater inside Component not instantiated until createObject — pool pattern preferred
NumberAnimation onStopped does not fire reliably at zero effective duration — wrap in SequentialAnimation with PauseAnimation { duration: 1 } before ScriptAction
QML property lookup only walks to file root — child items cannot resolve unqualified property names from intermediate parent Items

QtPositioning.coordinate() does not deep-copy when passed another coordinate object or its .latitude/.longitude properties — the result may retain a live reference to the source. Workaround: force value snapshot by adding +0 to each component: QtPositioning.coordinate(loc.latitude+0, loc.longitude+0, loc.altitude). The arithmetic coerces the QML binding into a primitive at that instant.
layer.enabled on a child does not prevent opacity inheritance from parent — to keep child at full opacity while parent fades, make child a sibling not a child

Conditional anchors (switching between undefined and real targets at runtime) are unreliable — binding engine does not cleanly release anchors. Use two separate items with visibility switching instead.
property var array mutation (unshift, index assignment) does not emit changed signal — always reassign: arr = arr after mutation to force binding re-evaluation
Connections deprecated onFoo syntax — use function onFoo() { } syntax in all new code

OpacityMask forces compositor layer every frame. Acceptable cost when: (1) the alternative requires equally expensive workarounds, (2) Qt likely pays similar internal cost for rounded Rectangle clipping anyway, (3) visual consistency with other components using OpacityMask outweighs the cost. Avoid in tight game loops or high-frequency animations. Confirmed acceptable in IntSelector track after co-maintainer review.

Qt.createQmlObject Timer antipattern: creating Timers via Qt.createQmlObject inline string injection in functions allocates heap objects requiring explicit destroy() calls, creates double-destroy race risks, and adds GC pressure. Replace with declared static Timer children at root level — start/stop/reset via method calls. Confirmed performance improvement in asteroid-dodger.

svg_rendering.qt515_svg_static_only: Qt 5.15 SVG renderer implements SVG Tiny 1.2 only. CSS @keyframes animations are silently ignored — SVG renders at t=0 frame only. No animation cost incurred.
svg_rendering.qt515_svg_no_mask: <mask> elements are silently ignored in Qt 5.15 — all layers render fully visible. Meteocon-style depth layering (front shape punching hole in back shape) will not render correctly.
svg_rendering.qt515_svg_use_unresolved: <use> elements referencing single-letter IDs in <defs> (e.g. #b, #d) produce 'qt.svg: link #b is undefined' errors in journald and render nothing. Flatten SVGs with Inkscape before deploying. Confirmed failure: meteocon SVGs on catfish.
svg_rendering.inkscape_1x_flatten_command: inkscape --actions='select-all;clone-unlink;object-to-path' --export-type=svg --export-filename=out.svg in.svg — flattens <use> references into inline geometry. Note: pre-1.0 Inkscape uses --verb and --export-plain-svg (deprecated). Actions-based syntax is 1.x only.
svg_rendering.chromium_headless_svg_frame: chromium --headless --screenshot --virtual-time-budget=N --window-size=W,H --default-background-color=0 'file://path.svg' — seeks CSS animations to Nms before capture. Only viable tool for exporting a specific animation frame without npm.
svg_rendering.qt67_svg_mask_support: Qt 6.7 adds <mask> and <filter> element support to QtSvg — meteocon-style depth masking renders correctly from 6.7 onwards.
svg_rendering.qt610_svg_animation_support: Qt 6.10 adds CSS @keyframes animation support to QtSvg for transforms, colors and opacities — full animated meteocon rendering requires Qt 6.10+.
svg_rendering.qt612_lts_eta: Qt 6.12 is the next LTS after 6.8 (every 4th minor = LTS). Expected ~late 2026. First version combining mask support + CSS animation + LTS stability.

ssl_clock_dependency.description: Qt XMLHttpRequest HTTPS connections fail silently with status:0 and onerror if the system clock is significantly wrong. SSL certificate validation requires the clock to be within the certificate validity window. Ping succeeds (ICMP, no SSL) while HTTPS fails — this asymmetry is the diagnostic. Fix: set system clock correctly via NTP or ssh date sync. On freshly flashed devices before first NTP sync the clock may be wrong causing all HTTPS requests in QML to fail. openssl s_client will succeed even with wrong clock in some builds — do not use it as the definitive SSL diagnostic.

rubyfish_qt_network_broken.description: rubyfish (TicWatch Pro 3) 2.1 release build has a broken Qt network stack — HTTPS XMLHttpRequest fails with status:0 despite openssl s_client succeeding, CA certs present, and correct system clock. find /usr/lib/qt5 returns no such directory on rubyfish while the same command on catfish nightly returns Qt plugin paths. Probable cause: missing Qt TLS plugin in the rubyfish image. Reported to MagneFire who maintains the rubyfish port. Not a code issue — store functionality confirmed working on catfish, beluga, and sparrow with correct clock.

usb_host_side._captured: 2026-07-12, from the asteroid-docking-bay sessions (host-side USB power management for watch fleets)
usb_host_side.kernel_per_port_power: The kernel exposes per-port hub power directly: /sys/bus/usb/devices/<hubloc>:1.0/<hubloc>-port<N>/disable (write 0=on, 1=off) — a single targeted operation. uhubctl by contrast re-enumerates the whole USB tree via libusb on EVERY invocation (5-13s on a deep cascade) and its concurrent scans race adb's libusb use. Rule of thumb: sysfs for the hot switching path, uhubctl for discovery/mapping only. Read-back of the disable attr does a live GetPortStatus (honest), but registers can't see everything: physical per-port buttons on some hubs (RSHTech A16) cut VBUS below all software visibility — register says on, port is dark; LEDs are the truth there. Per-port over_current_count sysfs attrs exist for real OCP diagnosis.
usb_host_side.port_off_on_needs_cycle: Hubs are not guaranteed to raise a connect event after a plain off->on write; a stale dark node can block re-enumeration. A single-invocation power CYCLE (uhubctl -a cycle, or sysfs off/sleep/on) makes the hub signal properly — this is the stale-node recovery primitive.
usb_host_side.udev_rootless_pattern: Rootless port switching: udev rule with GROUP="users" + TAG+="uaccess" for device access (plugdev does NOT exist on Arch-family distros — a rules file using it silently does nothing), plus a RUN+= that chgrp/chmods each hub port's sysfs disable attr on hub add. 'udevadm trigger --action=add' applies to already-plugged hubs. Gotcha: group membership needs a FULL re-login — long-running systemd user managers keep the old group set, so services stay in fallback until logout/login.
usb_host_side.adb_server_binding: The adb server binds 127.0.0.1:5037 only. Containers cannot reach the host adb server via host.containers.internal (confirmed by probe); `adb -a` would listen on the LAN (usually the wrong trade). ADB_SERVER_SOCKET=tcp:HOST:PORT redirects a client. In containers, running adb inside (with /dev/bus/usb passed through) is the clean default; AsteroidOS watches being auth-less makes the second keyring free.
usb_host_side.adb_devices_l_parsing: `adb devices -l` extras (usb:PATH product: model: device: transport_id:) give the physical USB path per serial — a genuine host-side mapping upgrade. Parser trap: daemon-restart notices ('* daemon started...') appear BEFORE the 'List of devices attached' header; naive line-splitting turns them into bogus device entries. Skip to the header and ignore '*' lines.
usb_host_side.podman_gotchas: (1) ReadOnly rootfs + podman secrets conflict: the default /run/secrets mountpoint cannot be created on a read-only rootfs — target the secret into /tmp (tmpfs) instead: Secret=name,type=mount,target=/tmp/name. (2) A Python process as container PID 1 gets no default signal dispositions — without an explicit SIGTERM handler every stop burns the runtime's 10s kill timeout. (3) Rootless container port-forwards (pasta/slirp) squat host ports invisibly for months — a service failing EADDRINUSE on 8080 should check `ss -tlnp` for pasta.
usb_host_side.enumeration_storm: Powering many watch ports simultaneously (e.g. a 16-port hub cycling to all-on) causes an enumeration storm; historically wedged the adb server on a 5-chip RTS5411 cascade (0.3 era), though a 5-watch storm passed cleanly on the 0.4/0.5 stack. Staggered power-on remains the safe pattern for large fleets. uhubctl is AUR-only on Arch-family (not in repos).
usb_host_side.adb_server_wedge_and_interface_detection: The host adb SERVER can WEDGE — list nothing from `adb devices` while watches are still enumerated on the USB bus (seen live 2026-07-24 on the w541 rig: powered ports, LEDs lit, watches present in sysfs, adb blind; the whole fleet looked dead). `adb kill-server && adb start-server` recovers it. To DETECT the wedge independently of the server, read the bus from sysfs: a watch offering adb advertises the standard Android ADB USB interface — a `{devpath}:*` interface dir with bInterfaceClass=ff, bInterfaceSubClass=42, bInterfaceProtocol=01. Key on THAT, not on idProduct: the fleet enumerates adb as 18d1:d001 (TicWatch Pro / Triggerfish / ASUS ZenWatch 2 all confirmed), NOT the 0a03 that usb_moded/dyn-modes and older detectors assume (0a02 is developer_mode/SSH). So a self-heal that counts 'adb-mode devices in sysfs the server can't see' must use the interface signature. a-d-b's warmer now does this (audit A2), guarded: wedge must persist across two 5s checks (avoid racing a just-plugged watch) and restarts at most once/60s (a restart briefly drops every watch).
usb_host_side.drain_no_suspend_launcher_pulseaudio: ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-24 on the w541 rig: watches that historically held 6-8 DAYS standby drained in 2-4 HOURS (22-36%/h) with the SCREEN OFF. NOT AoD (mcetool showed Display state=off, Blank inhibit=disabled), NOT the speaker (fast-drainers HAS_SPEAKER=true; no-speaker hypothesis disproven), NOT a-d-b. Cause: asteroid-launcher holds an open pulseaudio SINK-INPUT, so `pactl list short sinks` shows sink.primary RUNNING (not SUSPENDED) even on an idle screen-off watch; a running sink keeps the audio DSP/hardware clocked, which blocks SoC suspend → the SoC never enters LPM and drains at ~display-on rates. module-suspend-on-idle is loaded but cannot idle a sink that has a live stream. This is the 'pulseaudio won't let it sleep' / Qt6-migration issue — a shared-code (asteroid-launcher / pulseaudio) matter for the maintainers, not a per-device or docking-bay bug. Diagnostic recipe: on the watch (su ceres, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000) `pactl list short sinks` (RUNNING=awake), `pactl list short sink-inputs` (shows the launcher's stream), and `cat /sys/kernel/debug/wakeup_sources | awk '$9>0'` (mce_cpu_keepalive held). IMPLICATION for any drain/battery measurement: a drain test on such a watch measures the no-suspend rate, not standby — fix the launcher sleep bug before trusting standby numbers.
usb_host_side.hub_power_budget_brownout: ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-23 with live a-d-b data on the A16-class 16-port USB-A hub: it browns out at ~8 powered watches (8th flaky, 9th hard-fails) — powered ports register on but watches can't boot/enumerate, and watches that were already up DROP as more ports are energised. a-d-b's usb_volt is the diagnostic: healthy ports ~5.06V, loaded ports sag to 4.30V, some float ~6.0V, some collapse to ~0V (watch then runs on battery, invisible). The 4.3-6.0V spread = weak/absent internal 5V regulation. PSU RULED OUT: 12V/8A/96W brick runs cool/barely-loaded, so the hub draws only ~15-25W total and chokes current in its own 12V->5V converter + 5V distribution + per-port switches, delivering ~a quarter of its '60W' sticker. Per-watch ~2W idle but boot/display/radio/charge transient is 2-4x that, so the POWER-ON spike (not steady state) tips the rail -> power on ONE AT A TIME. Rules: ~7-8 watches/hub hard ceiling; split across INDEPENDENT hubs for more concurrency; a browned watch's drain data is garbage. a-d-b reads usb_volt already, so a brownout guard (warn on VBUS<~4.6V across powered ports; refuse the Nth) is cheap. This is the resolution of the long-running 'dock quirks = brownout?' thread: the hub's 5V stage is the limit, not the PSU or the watches.

device_screen_geometry.source_of_truth: qml-asteroid DeviceSpecs (src/utils/src/devicespecs.cpp) reads /etc/asteroid/machine.conf as a QSettings IniFormat file. This is THE canonical per-device spec source — a freshly ported watch ships it, so read it over adb instead of maintaining any per-codename table on the host side.
device_screen_geometry.machine_conf_keys: [Display] ROUND (bool -> hasRoundScreen), FLAT_TIRE (int px chin height, 0=none, Moto360-style), BORDER_GESTURE_WIDTH (float, default 0.1), NEEDS_BURN_IN_PROTECTION (bool). [Capabilities] HAS_WLAN, HAS_SPEAKER, HAS_MIC (bool; absent == false, so a watch can have a mic but no speaker). [Identity] MACHINE (the codename). Also /etc/hostname and /etc/os-release BUILD_ID are read by DeviceSpecs.
device_screen_geometry.resolution_source: Use /sys/class/graphics/fb0/modes ('U:360x360p-2640' -> regex \d+x\d+ = true panel resolution). Do NOT use /sys/class/graphics/fb0/virtual_size: it is DOUBLE-BUFFERED (reports 360,720 for a 360x360 panel), so its height is wrong. Confirmed live on skipjack 2026-07-17: machine.conf ROUND=true, MACHINE=skipjack; modes=360x360; virtual_size=360,720.
device_screen_geometry.why_it_matters: Lets a fleet/host tool determine screen shape (round/square/flat-tire) and true resolution for masking screenshots (round->circle) and for distinguishing same-shape watches by size that a codename cannot: tunny 400 vs skipjack 360 (both round); belugaxl 476x402 vs beluga 320x360 (belugaxl runs the beluga image, so codename is ambiguous but the live resolution disambiguates). There is no canonical published AsteroidOS resolution table, so reading fb0/modes is the reliable way to verify actual resolution, including on freshly ported unknown watches.
device_screen_geometry.found_by: asteroid-docking-bay 0.7 screen-geometry feature, 2026-07-17 (mo + Claude). Reading the file on-watch over adb is fine; this is NOT patching qml-asteroid.

usb_mode_switch_and_ssh.summary: AsteroidOS USB gadget mode is controlled by usb_moded. Switch it with `usb_moded_util -s <mode>` (adb_mode / developer_mode / mtp_mode / charging_only). adb_mode enumerates idProduct 0a03; developer_mode (SSH) enumerates 0a02. The shipped default boot mode was recently changed to adb_mode (releases are for users; devs toggle).
usb_mode_switch_and_ssh.usb_ssh_reachability: CONFIRMED live on the w541 rig 2026-07-18: switch a watch adb->developer_mode via `adb -s SER shell usb_moded_util -s developer_mode`; after ~9s the host gets an rndis link (host side 192.168.2.1) and the watch is reachable at root@192.168.2.15 (fixed /24, ONE such watch at a time). `ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o BatchMode=yes root@192.168.2.15 '<cmd>'` runs commands on the watch (root, key-based, no host network setup needed — the earlier 'needs DHCP/host setup' claim was a stale glitch). Switch back with `ssh root@192.168.2.15 usb_moded_util -s adb_mode`, or a port power-cycle reboots to the adb_mode default (so a stranded-SSH watch self-recovers).
usb_mode_switch_and_ssh.adb_vs_ssh_transport: For a host-side fleet tool, adb and ssh are interchangeable transports: `adb -s SER shell X` and `ssh root@IP X` both forward the SAME quoted remote command X to a shell on the watch, so a Transport abstraction only swaps the prefix (files: adb pull/push vs scp -r). asteroid-docking-bay 0.8 does exactly this (transport.py) — every Watch feature works over either link. Two SSH kinds: USB-SSH (192.168.2.15 over rndis) and WiFi-SSH (the watch's WiFi IP); both can be active at once.
usb_mode_switch_and_ssh.remote_command_quoting_trap: adb_shell and SshTransport.shell run with shell=True on the HOST, so any remote command containing a glob, pipe, redirect or ';' MUST be passed as one double-quoted string (f'"{cmd}"') or the host shell parses it: pipes/redirects execute host-side and globs expand against the HOST's /sys before adb/ssh ever forwards to the watch. Bitten TWICE in a-d-b, both caught only on hardware: (1) battery_and_screen's `mcetool | grep` pipeline ran mcetool on the host, so a stuck screen read 'fine'; (2) get_battery_level grew a `nanohub_fuelgauge-*` glob (921b713, 2026-07-13) that the host expanded to its own BAT0, handing the watch a path it lacked — the read returned None and silently broke drain-start AND the charge loop for 11 days, while the UI stayed fine because it reads over the already-quoted battery_and_screen path. The failure was FLAKY not blanket: an unmatched host glob is kept literal and a host-side `| head -1` grabs whichever of the watch's error line vs digit arrives first, so some watches read fine and others returned None. Rule: quote any remote pipeline as a unit, and unit-test it by asserting the command handed to the shell starts and ends with '"' — a path-priority or output-parse test does NOT catch host-side leakage, which is exactly what let (2) ship. Fixed 2026-07-24 (a-d-b 0.9).

adb_vs_ssh_performance.observation: SSH-over-USB is dramatically slower than adb for the same per-watch operation — mo measured opening the Control Center in SSH mode ~5x slower than in adb mode (2026-07-22).
adb_vs_ssh_performance.cause: asteroid-docking-bay's SshTransport runs a fresh `ssh {opts} root@<ip> <cmd>` per call, so every command pays a full TCP + SSH handshake and key exchange. adb reuses one persistent daemon connection, so its per-command overhead is near zero. The Control Center is one batched shell script, so it is a single ssh handshake — but that one handshake still dominates versus adb's warm channel.
adb_vs_ssh_performance.consequence: SSH is a correct FULL functional replacement for adb (Control Center, toggles, poweroff all work over it — see _reachable_transport / _watch), but it is not a performance equal. Prefer adb when both are available; SSH is the fallback for a watch deliberately in developer mode or when only the WiFi/rndis link is up.
adb_vs_ssh_performance.future_optimization: SSH ControlMaster + ControlPersist would multiplex a persistent connection and amortise the handshake across calls (add `-o ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPath=... -o ControlPersist=30s` to _SSH_OPTS). Not yet done — noted as the obvious speedup if SSH-mode usage grows.

usb_ip_assignment.summary: The rndis/SSH address is set with usb_moded_util -n set:ip,<addr>. CONFIRMED live on skipjack 2026-07-22: the IP does NOT change under a live SSH/developer session — set:ip only takes effect on the next transition INTO developer_mode. So it must be set while the watch is on adb, then applied by switching to developer_mode.
usb_ip_assignment.why_it_matters: Every developer_mode watch defaults to the SailfishOS-inherited 192.168.2.15, so two watches switched to SSH on one rig collide on the same address across different host interfaces and become unaddressable. asteroid-docking-bay 0.8 hands each serial a sticky unique IP from 192.168.13.37 (LEET) via allocate_ssh_ip, set over adb inside the watch.switch_ssh op before the switch.
usb_ip_assignment.relocation_is_a_round_trip: Moving a watch already stranded on the shared 192.168.2.15 onto its unique IP cannot be done in place (IP frozen under live SSH). It is a round-trip built from two existing ops, no new device code: _switch_ssh_to_adb(.15) -> wait for adb -> watch.switch_ssh(serial) (allocate + set:ip + developer_mode). Verified end-to-end on skipjack: .15 -> 13.37, .15 freed, net-zero.
usb_ip_assignment.stray_detection: A watch in SSH mode whose ssh_ip_for_serial is None MUST be on the default .15, because a non-default IP only exists via allocate_ssh_ip inside switch_ssh. So SSH-mode + no allocation cleanly identifies an accidental stray vs a deliberately-switched watch (always allocated) — no network probe needed. a-d-b auto-aligns strays to the usb_mode_preference toggle (webstatus._maybe_align_usb_mode), guarded like the fake-power self-heal.
usb_ip_assignment.open_question: Whether set:ip persists across a watch REBOOT is unverified as of 2026-07-22 — deferred as an acceptable exception since the auto-align catches a reverted watch on its next poll.
usb_ip_assignment.confidence: confirmed live on skipjack (a-d-b 0.8 SSH-IP work)

provider_reference_leak_and_coldstart_bu.description: AsteroidOS ships geoclue1 (0.12.99, Garmin/OpenedHand 2007-08, dead upstream, dbus-glib) because geoclue2 dropped out-of-process providers, which watch-specific GPS daemons (e.g. dodoradio's casiowsd) need. The geoclue1 master daemon was abandoned mid-refactor and has NO working provider dereference path: GcMasterClient Add/RemoveReference are TODO no-ops, the master never destroys client objects nor watches app bus names, and the provider shutdown in gc_master_provider_unsubscribe() is commented out (master-provider.c:1073). Net effect: once the master references a GPS provider it never sends RemoveReference, so the provider refcount (keyed to the master's own never-dying bus name) never empties and the GPS module stays powered forever after the app exits.
provider_reference_leak_and_coldstart_bu.second_latent_bug: Re-enabling the shutdown exposes a cold-start bug: gc_master_client_get_best_provider() unsubscribes ALL candidates when none is AVAILABLE yet - a cold-starting GPS is in ACQUIRING, so the master kills it within a second of starting it (field-observed: activate -> options -> 'shut down casiowsd' in one journal second). This is why the 2008 author disabled shutdown instead of fixing selection; their own TODO admits it. Fix: keep not-yet-available candidates subscribed so status-changed re-triggers selection on fix acquisition.
provider_reference_leak_and_coldstart_bu.fix: Cumulative patch (field-tested on medaka 2026-07-19: cold start acquires AND provider shuts down on app close): real per-sender refcounting on GcMasterClient mirroring gc-provider.c, NameOwnerChanged watch for crashed apps, client self-destruction at zero refs (idle-deferred), re-enabled deinitialize, and no-unsubscribe-while-waiting in get_best_provider. Needs dbus-glib >= 0.90. Patch: mo ~/Git/geoclue1-master-refleak_v2.patch; to be carried in the distro geoclue recipe.
provider_reference_leak_and_coldstart_bu.design_rules_for_any_replacement: Two MUSTs any location middleware (e.g. the proposed geovibe2.5 geoclue2 fork) must encode and planted-bug-test: (1) a provider MUST keep running while ACQUIRING if any client waits on it; (2) a provider MUST power down when its last referencing client leaves the bus, politely or by crashing. Keep geoclue2's client wire API so Qt's stock geoclue2 position plugin works unmodified; innovate only on the provider-plugin side.

qt6_build_infrastructure_lessons.note: Hard-won 2026-07-18/19 during the first full skipjack qt6 image builds on the refreshed w541 (Arch host). All confirmed through repeated full builds.
qt6_build_infrastructure_lessons.buildtools_mandatory_on_modern_hosts: Bare-metal walnascar builds FAIL on hosts with gcc 16 (cannot compile gcc-cross 14.3's libcody: C++20 char8_t mismatch). Fix: Yocto buildtools-extended tarball (src/oe-core/scripts/install-buildtools, source its environment-setup BEFORE prepare-build.sh, every invocation). Bonus: buildtools ships its own CA bundle - the w541's broken host cert store made every AUTOREV git ls-remote fail with 'SSL certificate problem', which MASQUERADES as random per-recipe parse ExpansionErrors and was misdiagnosed as GitHub rate limiting until the full error text was read. Rule: always read the complete fetcher error before theorizing.
qt6_build_infrastructure_lessons.cmake_native_libidn2_walnascar_backport: cmake-native fails do_compile under buildtools when the host has libidn2 (CMake finds /usr/lib/libidn2.so + records /usr/include, then omits -I/usr/include as 'implicit' - wrong for a sysrooted compiler). Upstream fix 861eaeb79f (-DCMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_Libidn2=ON) exists on master/wrynose but NOT walnascar. CRITICAL: walnascar's cmake-native takes configure args via CMAKE_EXTRACONF, not EXTRA_OECMAKE (the variable the upstream fix patches in 4.3.1) - appending to the wrong variable does not even change the taskhash.
qt6_build_infrastructure_lessons.systemctl_native_pam_contamination: systemd-systemctl-native fails do_compile under buildtools on hosts shipping PAM headers in /usr/include (Arch does; Debian's -dev split hides it): meson probes find host PAM, sysrooted compiler cannot include security/pam_ext.h. Fix: EXTRA_OEMESON += "-Dpam=disabled" (PAM is irrelevant to the native systemctl helper). No upstream fix as of 2026-07 - reportable to oe-core.
qt6_build_infrastructure_lessons.image_install_append_is_global: IMAGE_INSTALL:append in local.conf applies to EVERY image recipe including initramfs-android-image - appending apps bloated the initramfs from ~40MB to 217MB and failed INITRAMFS_MAXSIZE. Always scope: IMAGE_INSTALL:append:pn-asteroid-image.
qt6_build_infrastructure_lessons.autorev_pathologies: AUTOREV failure modes observed in one night: (1) mid-build upstream movement re-resolves the rev and can silently orphan workdir overlays; (2) parse-time git ls-remote storms (~200 recipes) make every bitbake invocation network-dependent and slow; (3) any transient TLS/network failure kills the whole parse with cryptic ExpansionErrors. Mitigations: BB_SRCREV_POLICY = "cache" in local.conf (reuse last successful resolution), BBMASK for recipe groups not in play, and ultimately pinned SRCREVs (project rule).
qt6_build_infrastructure_lessons.fish_login_shell_cannot_source_yocto: prepare-build.sh requires bash/zsh as the SOURCING shell; fish parses it with fish grammar and dies (also inside tmux windows, whose default-shell is the login shell). Wrap all remote build work: ssh host bash -s <<'EOF' and tmux new-session "bash /abs/script.sh".

device_flashing.simg_when_in_doubt: WHEN IN DOUBT, SIMG. Some watches will NOT boot from a raw ext4 flashed to userdata and need an Android sparse image instead. Known simg-required devices: medaka, tetra, pike, mooneye (raw ext4 gives the AsteroidOS logo briefly then a black screen with no adb/ssh; medaka confirmed 2026-07-23). Most other watches (e.g. skipjack) take a pure raw .ext4 directly. Convert with `ext2simg <rootfs.ext4> <rootfs.simg>` (or the fs-agnostic `img2simg`), then `fastboot flash userdata rootfs.simg`. Always worth a test when a freshly flashed watch will not boot.
device_flashing.why_device_specific: It is a per-device bootloader/partition property, NOT the image size: medaka/tetra/pike/mooneye require the sparse format for a correct userdata write, while skipjack-class devices accept raw ext4 directly. (fastboot does auto-sparse any image that exceeds the device max-download-size, shown as `Sending sparse 'userdata' 2/3 …`, but that is only a transfer-chunking detail and is not why these four need simg.) The sparse flash also reports `skip copying userdata image avb footer due to sparse image`.
device_flashing.sparse_format: Android sparse (simg) is a container describing the fs as chunks — RAW (real data), FILL (a repeated value such as a run of zeros stored as one record), DONT_CARE (unallocated). It never stores zero runs literally, so it is smaller and is the format device flashing expects. simg2img reverses it; not directly mountable.
device_flashing.beluga_is_a_separate_case: BELUGA IS DIFFERENT and is NOT a simg case — do not lump it with skipjack. Beluga has an ENCRYPTED HOME and needs a special flash procedure to circumvent it (dodo): enter fastboot, `fastboot -w` (wipe userdata/cache), reboot, then the device prompts to push asteroidos.ext4 via adb. dodo's phrase 'medaka has a beluga-like install' referred to THIS procedure; it turned out medaka does NOT need it and flashes like any normal watch. Keep beluga's encrypted-home procedure separate from the simg-vs-raw-ext4 axis.
device_flashing.medaka_install: medaka (dodo's Casio port) flashes like a normal watch: convert the rootfs to .simg and `fastboot flash userdata rootfs.simg`, then reboot — NOT the beluga procedure. Enter fastboot: top button, hold the middle button until the screen goes white, then release middle while holding top.

nemo_configuration_dconf_types.issue: Writing AsteroidOS Nemo-Configuration (MGConfItem/ConfigurationValue) keys over `dconf write` from a host must match the gvariant TYPE the QML expects, or the value reads back empty/absent. Cost a real debugging session (docking-bay 2026-07-23).
nemo_configuration_dconf_types.scalars: bool/int/string keys (e.g. /org/asteroidos/settings/use-12h-format, .../burn-in-protection-level) are bare: `dconf write /key true` | `... 30` | `... "'text'"`. Fine as a{sb}-style bare literals.
nemo_configuration_dconf_types.dicts: A DICT key is stored as a QVariantMap = gvariant a{sv} (variant-WRAPPED values), NOT a{sb}. Write `dconf write /desktop/asteroid/quickpanel/enabled "{'lockButton': <true>, 'musicButton': <false>}"` (angle-bracket <> around each value). A plain a{sb} `{'x': true}` write reads back EMPTY in the launcher -> QuickPanel builds an empty panel. Verified both directions on skipjack.
nemo_configuration_dconf_types.read_parse: When PARSING a `dconf dump` of such a dict, accept the <...> wrapper: regex `'([^']+)'\s*:\s*<?(true|false)>?`. An a{sb}-only parser reads every value as absent and the UI shows defaults over the real state.
nemo_configuration_dconf_types.defaults_gap: There is NO GSettings SCHEMA on the watch for /org/asteroidos/settings/* (verified: `gsettings list-schemas | grep asteroid` = nothing). So `dconf read` returns EMPTY for any key still at its default and `gsettings get` fails; the effective default lives in the asteroid-settings QML `defaultValue` and must be baked host-side. (Weather keys DO have a schema: org.asteroidos.weather + .dayN.)
nemo_configuration_dconf_types.session_bus: dconf as the watch UI user needs its session bus: as ceres run with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000 DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus HOME=/home/ceres`. From root adb: `su ceres -c '<env> dconf ...'`.

narwhal_hands_movement.device: narwhal (LG Watch W7) has a physical soprod movement exposed at /sys/devices/sop716/ (i2c soprod_movement). Only current hands-watch in the fleet.
narwhal_hands_movement.set_hands: To MOVE the hands, write a local datetime `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` to /sys/devices/sop716/time as root; the movement driver follows it. This is exactly what dodoradio's narwhal-hands-timesync writes (Qt ISODate date + TextDate time). tz_minutes = offset/60 to /sys/devices/sop716/tz_minutes. init.rc also writes motor_move_all "45:135" at boot (raw homing) and chmods motor_move* to 222 (write-only), position to 444 (read-only).
narwhal_hands_movement.motor_move_all: DECODED ON HARDWARE 2026-07-23 (supervised bench test on narwhal <serial>, mo eyeballing): `echo "M:H" > /sys/devices/sop716/motor_move_all` (write-only). Format is minute:hour (M drives the MINUTE hand, H the HOUR hand — confirmed by moving one field at a time). Each value is 0..179 = ABSOLUTE angle at 180 units per full revolution (1 unit = 2 degrees, 3 units = one minute-mark). It is ABSOLUTE and RE-SYNCS the counter: after the write, /sys/devices/sop716/position reads back exactly the written value, and the physical hands go there — so a single motor_move_all is the RE-HOME that cures open-loop timepiece-mode drift (no minute-nudge needed). There is a small fixed motor-zero offset (value 0 landed both hands ~17-18 min-mark, not 12 o'clock) and NO minute snap — resolution is sub-minute (2 deg), hands rest between ticks. min-mark ~= (offset + value/3) mod 60. init.rc homes to "45:135" at boot. Choreography = sequence motor_move_all writes (independent hands: corners/sweep/scissor), then a `time` write to restore the clock. motor_init/reset/motor_move also exist (write-only, chmod 222) but were not needed once motor_move_all proved absolute+resyncing.
narwhal_hands_movement.position_read: /sys/devices/sop716/position reads the driver's tracked hand position as `M:H` (same minute:hour unit as motor_move_all, 0..179 each). It is the driver's OPEN-LOOP counter, not a sensor read — in timepiece mode (low battery, no OS) the MCU steps the hands with no feedback and the counter DRIFTS from the physical hands (observed 3h+ off: counter 87:82 while hands at 20:42). So a bare position read is unreliable for a real-vs-ideal readout UNTIL a motor_move_all write re-syncs it (after which position == the commanded value and matches physical). Other files: battery_level (mV), time, tz_minutes, watch_mode (1 at boot), version, self_test, aging_test.
narwhal_hands_movement.confidence: set_hands + motor_move_all format/unit/absolute-resync CONFIRMED on hardware 2026-07-23 (supervised, mo eyeballing); exact motor-zero offset approximate (no minute snap)

yocto_host_contamination.principle: Yocto's host isolation covers INCLUDE paths more thoroughly than LINKER SEARCH paths. A find_package/meson probe that looks for a library can therefore succeed against the HOST library while the matching header stays invisible — configure passes and the COMPILE dies on a missing header. Suspect this shape whenever a -native recipe fails on a header for a library the host happens to have installed.

known_cases.cmake-native / libidn2: Vendored curl does an unconditional set(USE_LIBIDN2 ON) then find_package(Libidn2); an Arch host has libidn2 by default. Fix in build/conf/local.conf: CMAKE_EXTRACONF:append:pn-cmake-native = " -DCMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_Libidn2=ON"  — MUST be CMAKE_EXTRACONF, NOT EXTRA_OECMAKE: cmake-native bootstraps itself with its own do_configure and never reads EXTRA_OECMAKE, so setting that variable changes nothing and looks like a failed fix.
known_cases.systemd-systemctl-native / PAM: Meson finds /usr/lib/libpam.so on the host and enables PAM; compile then fails on security/pam_ext.h. Fix: EXTRA_OEMESON:append:pn-systemd-systemctl-native = " -Dpam=disabled"
